text:
maria: hit a customer report this morning: resumed SSE streams sometimes emit duplicated partial chunks and billing shows double tokens for the resumed window. Repro on two tenants.

jb: paste logs? specifically want resume token and Last-Event-ID flow.

maria: heres a trimmed log snippet:
```
INFO stream: client=acct-112 resume_token=rtk-9a1 received_resume
INFO stream: server: accept_resume seq=572
EMIT chunk id=572.partA
EMIT chunk id=572.partA  <-- duplicate
billing: charge tokens=+92 (resumed)
```

evan: probable cause: resume path replays cached KV events while the normal request pipeline also processes the resumed request and increments billing. Two independent counters.

lucy: sounds like a race in gating: after accept_resume we still enqueue a fresh request that hits billing layer; concurrently resume replay emits the cached tokens.

kevin: on Console we see a per-route token spike but the stream timeline has no visible gap to justify it. Console aggregates from two ingestion points (edge and core) so we're double-counting there too. Need to dedupe upstream.

maria: repro steps I used:
1) start SSE stream -> generate ~150 tokens -> simulate network cut
2) reconnect with Last-Event-ID header set to server id
3) server accepts resume, replays cached output + also runs resume through normal pipeline
4) client gets duplicate partial chunk, console/billing increment twice

jb: curl test to reproduce:
```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Last-Event-ID: 572" https://api.redwood/streams/gen?model=redwood-lite
```

ops-bot: deploy/stream-resume-probe -> staging green (hash: c3b7a1). Tests added: resume-idempotency, billing-dup-check 

sre-bot: alert: 3 high error-rate incidents linked to stream resume in last 45m (affected: us-west-2 gateway pool)

kevin: two candidate fixes: 
- Option A: formal resume handshake that returns resume_session_id and make billing idempotent by resume_session_id + seq window.
- Option B: short-term: block billing increments for N seconds after resume accept for that session so replayed events aren't charged.

lucy: A is cleaner but touches billing semantics and maybe DB schema. B is invasive but faster to ship. We need telemetry to measure scope before changing billing contracts.

maria: telemetry wishlist:
- metric: stream_resume_attempts
- metric: stream_resume_dup_event_count (count of duplicated token chunk ids)
- trace attribute: resume_session_id
- Console: mark resumed sessions in the timeline and show "resume delta tokens"

evan: alternative: support client-supplied resume_id (idempotency token) in resume request. Server uses that as dedupe key. Backwards-compatible if optional. Minimal server state if clients provide token.

jb: support both: prefer client resume_id if present, otherwise server issues resume_session_id in accept response. Billing only counts resumed payload once per resume_id/session.

lucy: Console UX: show a small "resumed" pill on stream sessions with tooltip: "resumed at seq N 6 tokens billed on resume" and a link to resume_session_id trace.

maria: action items:
- evan: add metrics and trace tag behind a feature flag (1 day)
- kevin: prototype resume_id header + server dedupe (2 days) -> canary on dedicated region
- jb: add billing gate based on resume_session_id/resume_id (3 days)
- lucy: console annotate resumed sessions + dashboard delta (2 days)
- ops: enable staging canary and monitor stream_resume_dup_event_count

evan: pushing a quick metric to prod behind flag so we can quantify. hold on billing backfill until dedupe proven.

ops-bot: canary/stream-resume-dedupe enabled on dedicated-canary (us-west-2)

kevin: debate: require client to send resume_id or let server generate? If many SDKs already track session ids, client-supplied is simple. Server-generated reduces client burden but increases server state.

jb: implement dual mode: accept client resume_id if present, otherwise generate server resume_session_id and return it. Billing dedupe uses whichever id is present.

maria: ok, opening a postmortem draft and marking this P1 for billing correctness. Thanks all :thumbsup:
